componentPlan.focusQuote: The total aerodynamic force is equal to the pressure times the surface area around the body.
componentPlan.pedagogicalReason: Shows how pressure and surface area combine to form lift acting perpendicular to flight

componentPlan.focusQuote: The airplane on the left is shown in a cruise condition while the airplane on the right is shown in a takeoff or landing condition.
componentPlan.pedagogicalReason: Contrasts cruise and takeoff conditions to explain why wing area grows when velocity is low

componentPlan.focusQuote: We could, in theory, use the total surface area as the reference area.
componentPlan.pedagogicalReason: Checks recall of reference area choices and how size changes lift

overview.headline: How wing size and area shape lift in flight

keyPoints.point: Lift grows with wing area, so doubling area doubles lift force.
keyPoints.quote: Doubling the area doubles the lift.

keyPoints.point: Lift acts as the component of aerodynamic force perpendicular to flight direction.
keyPoints.quote: Lift is the component of this force perpendicular to the flight direction.

keyPoints.point: Total aerodynamic force equals pressure times surface area around the body.
keyPoints.quote: The total aerodynamic force is equal to the pressure times the surface area around the body.

keyPoints.point: Designers increase wing area by sliding flaps and shifting slats forward for takeoff and landing.
keyPoints.quote: This is done by sliding the flaps backwards along metal tracks and shifting the slats forward to increase the wing area.

keyTerms.gloss: aerodynamic force acting perpendicular to flight path
keyTerms.quote: Lift is an aerodynamic force and therefore depends on the pressure variation of the air around the body as it moves through the air.

keyTerms.gloss: other aerodynamic force directly linked to area
keyTerms.quote: Like the other aerodynamic force, drag, the lift is directly proportional to the area of the object.

keyTerms.gloss: wing area viewed from above used as reference area
keyTerms.quote: the logical choice is the wing planform area.

keyTerms.gloss: movable panels slid backwards to increase wing area
keyTerms.quote: This is done by sliding the flaps backwards along metal tracks and shifting the slats forward to increase the wing area.

analysis.pageCoverage: Explains how lift depends on size and pressure, how wing planform area serves as reference area, and how flaps and slats increase area for takeoff and landing.
